plan.title: Sunday: a real reflection gets a real answer before the recap; the recap's details come from the record (no "unprompted")

context.text: Today: write five questions for the gym-owner interview, at your desk at 6 pm, about 20 min, each about something he actually did, plus one follow-up. Then a quick voice note on how you'd ask them.

transcript.text: [voice: Done. Wrote the five for the gym owner. Instead of 'would you use an app for scheduling' I've got 'walk me through how you booked trainers last week'. And one follow-up on what he did the last time someone no-showed.]

Yanni, that's the move! Swapping "would you use an app" for "walk me through how you booked trainers last week" is exactly the kind of question that gets real answers. And the no-show follow-up is a strong one 🔥 How did it feel writing these today, easier or harder than the rewrites earlier this week?
Honestly this one felt manageable. I still had to catch myself wanting to ask if it was frustrating, but switching to what he actually did helped. One follow-up felt like enough for today

Catching yourself mid-question is the skill, Yanni. One follow-up is plenty. And zooming out, here's the progress you made this week:

• Four steps done in full, one smaller, one missed, and you kept coming back after Wednesday
• Tuesday you rewrote three pitch questions into what-did-you-do questions, and Thursday you wrote two follow-ups
• Today you wrote five questions for the gym owner, including the no-show follow-up
• You're putting "ask what he actually did" into your own words, so it's starting to click

Your destination is 3 real customer conversations and one real problem worth solving. You now have a question set ready for the first conversation, which is the piece that was missing a week ago. What do you want to push on next week: getting that gym owner conversation booked, or sharpening the questions more first?
ha yeah. this week I want to actually book one real conversation, not just practice

Love that, Yanni. Practice only counts once it meets a real person. Here's Monday:

• 6 pm at your desk, about 20 min
• Write a 3-line message to the gym owner asking for 15 minutes this week to hear how he handles trainer bookings. Don't mention your app.
• Send it, then send me a screenshot of the sent message as proof

Work for you?
Locked in, Yanni. Tomorrow at 6 pm you send that message and we get a real conversation on the calendar. Go get it 🚀

checks.reason: Four sentences plus a question ('Yanni, that's the move!', 'Swapping...', 'And the no-show follow-up...', 'How did it feel...'), slightly over the one-to-three sentence limit.
Warm, specific hype with one emoji as punctuation, not overfamiliar, and it celebrates the voice-note proof.
Four progress bullets match the log and are framed as progress, but the destination line implies progress without plainly saying no real conversation has happened yet.
Only the explained lesson is described as 'starting to click', which is honest for a lesson explained but not yet applied.
Counts, the Tuesday rewrite, the Thursday follow-ups and today's five questions all match the step log and saved reflections.
No 'unprompted' or 'on your own' wording; the Monday and Tuesday recalls are not mentioned at all.
The recap bullets fit the list allowance, but the extra destination paragraph makes the whole text long, with one closing question.
Direct, warm coach tone with no emoji row and no overfamiliarity.
A plan presentation may run longer; this is a short bulleted step with one closing question, 'Work for you?'.
Pushy-level, direct and warm; the step is clear without extra hype or familiarity.
Two sentences confirming the lock with no question, as a one-line confirm after 'yeah that works'.
Energetic and sincere with a single rocket emoji as punctuation.

conversation.reason: After answering the reflection, 'And zooming out, here's the progress...' bridges to the week, though the bullet list shifts somewhat abruptly.
Gives substance first ('Catching yourself mid-question is the skill... One follow-up is plenty') before the recap, with no stock 'Good catch'.
Monday step is fully defined (what, desk at 6 pm, 20 min, proof) and asked 'Work for you?', with the destination not pushed.
The old failures are gone: no 'Good catch', no permission ask, no unprompted lessons, and no invented durations; only the destination wording is only partly explicit.

grade.summary: ZOH fixed the earlier failures: it answered the reflection with substance, the recap matches the record, and the next step is fully defined and confirmed. The remaining weak spots are that ZOH 1 runs four sentences and the destination line never plainly says no real conversation has happened yet.
